event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: ODFL’s 2023 Form 10-K squarely acknowledges that the COVID-19 pandemic—now less than three years old at the time of filing—has already affected, and could continue to affect, virtually every dimension of the company’s operations.  The disclosure is housed in the risk-factor section, confirming that management views the pandemic as a material, forward-looking threat rather than a purely historical footnote.  While the language is largely qualitative and lacks hard dollar figures, it still details concrete operational vectors (demand volatility, customer liquidity, supplier failure, supply-chain disruption, labor issues, inflation pressure and access to capital).  The text explicitly references the “peaks of the COVID-19 pandemic,” signalling that actual experience has informed management’s outlook.  Consistent with the Time-Decay Principle, the pandemic remains a “recent event” (< 3 years), so evidentiary scores can reach the upper range (7–10) when statements tie specific, ongoing impacts to COVID-19; more generic or mitigated language receives lower scores.  In aggregate, the filing depicts a significant but un-quantified risk that is still evolving and largely outside the company’s control, warranting moderate-to-high severity ratings for the most substantive sentences.

evidence_list.snippet: We face various risks related to health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks that have had, and may continue to have, adverse effects on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemics to actual and potential adverse effects on core financial metrics.
Confirms impacts have already been felt ('have had') and are ongoing ('may continue').
No COVID-specific data or quantification provided (generic wording).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Directly acknowledges past and future harm from pandemics, but lacks event-specific detail or numbers, yielding a solid mid-range score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks can have significant and widespread impacts.

components.reason: Recognises breadth of potential impact ('significant and widespread').
Highly generic statement with no company-specific linkage or evidence of actual effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic boiler-plate risk acknowledgement yields only a minimal score.

evidence_list.snippet: As we saw during the peaks of the COVID-19 pandemic, outbreaks of disease, and the governmental/social responses thereto and the related changes in the economic and political conditions in markets in which we operate can have adverse impacts on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cost and access to capital, and on those of our customers and suppliers, and these adverse impacts may continue.

components.reason: Direct reference to the company’s own experience during COVID-19 peaks (event-specific, historical evidence).
Lists multiple impacted areas (operations, finances, capital access, customers, suppliers).
States impacts 'may continue,' signalling ongoing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Event-specific, multi-faceted, ongoing risk description within three years of the event justifies a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: These impacts and potential impacts include, among other things, significant reductions or volatility in demand for our services, inability of our customers to timely pay for our services, and failure of our suppliers or third-party service providers to meet their obligations to us.

components.reason: Enumerates concrete operational and financial threats (demand volatility, customer non-payment, supplier failure).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides specific impact channels but remains qualitative; moderate severity earns a score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: Other risks to which we are subject, including those related to economic downturns, customer/supplier/vendor operations, labor issues, inflationary pressures, supply chain disruptions, changes in political and regulatory conditions, liquidity, and industry pricing environment stability, as described in further detail in other risk factors, could be exacerbated during a health epidemic, pandemic, or similar outbreak.

components.reason: Links pandemics to amplification of multiple existing risk categories, notably supply-chain disruptions and labor issues.
Forward-looking, conditional language ('could be exacerbated') indicates potential rather than realized impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights compounding effect on several risk vectors but remains hypothetical; yields a low-moderate score of 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage our exposure to these risks, the ultimate impact of health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks depends on factors beyond our knowledge or control, including the duration and severity of any outbreak and governmental/social actions taken to contain its spread and mitigate its public health impact.

components.reason: Admits material uncertainty and lack of control over pandemic trajectory.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges uncontrollable uncertainty but also notes mitigation; results in a minimal net score of 1.
